newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast late spot products notionally higher.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast late spot products notionally higher.

text.p: U.S. West Coast distillate prices were notionally higher late, boosted by a rally in heating oil futures.
December heating oil settled up 2.95 cents a gallon at 71.20 cents as cold weather inspired the day's upswing in prices, ahead of a weekly U.S. inventory report.
ACCESS trade saw "heat" rising further, with the contract topping out at 72.15 cents a gallon within the first several hours of overnight trade.
Late bids for jet fuel in Los Angeles rose 0.50 cent to 68 cents a gallon.
Traders said support came from NYMEX and some lingering concerns supplies could tighten after a fire damaged a hydrotreater at Texaco's Wilmington, Calif., refinery.
The unit helps in the production of jet fuel.
Late prices for unleaded conventional gasoline in Los Angeles stayed at their early levels of 59/60 cents a gallon, while CARB-material held at 63.50/64.50 cents for November.
Traders said November activity faded as players rolled their positions into December, pushing bids for December CARB a half cent over November.

Wednesday's inventory report from the American Petroleum Institute (API) showed West Coast gasoline supplies up 533,000 barrels last week, lifting stocks 3.4 million barrels over the comparable period last year.
